issues.legal_issue: Police custody may be authorized only on a strong, judicially scrutinized showing that custody is necessary for further investigation.
material_facts: The accused had been granted bail before the police sought their custody for further investigation.
The complainant had settled the civil dispute and withdrawn her criminal complaint, while investigation was revived at the instance of a person unconnected with the dispute.
The police sought remand shortly after bail was granted, but the Magistrate gave no cogent reason why investigation could not proceed without police custody.
The accused had cooperated with the investigating authorities.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate and High Court were not justified in permitting police remand; the remand orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Police remand is an exception, not the rule. The investigating agency must establish a strong case and satisfy the Magistrate that further investigation cannot proceed without police custody; the Magistrate must judicially scrutinize the circumstances and give clear, cogent reasons. The Court relied on Article 22(2) of the Constitution and Sections 57 and 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as well as Chaganti Narayan Satyanarayan v. State of Andhra Pradesh and C.B.I. v. Anupam J. Kulkarni.

rule.if: police_remand_challenge_appeal and accused_already_on_bail and complainant_withdrew_after_settlement and investigation_revived_by_unconnected_person and magistrate_gave_no_cogent_necessity_reasons

predicates.police_remand_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order authorizing police custody for investigation.
predicates.accused_already_on_bail: The accused had been released on bail before police custody was sought.
predicates.complainant_withdrew_after_settlement: The complainant settled the underlying dispute and withdrew the complaint.
predicates.investigation_revived_by_unconnected_per: A person unconnected with the dispute caused the withdrawn complaint's investigation to resume.
predicates.magistrate_gave_no_cogent_necessity_reas: The Magistrate authorized police custody without explaining why investigation could not proceed without it.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges police custody authorized after bail, and the complaint had been withdrawn following settlement, an unconnected person revived the investigation, and the Magistrate gave no cogent reason for custody, the remand order is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: After a High Court has granted bail, a Magistrate cannot authorize police remand of the accused; the investigating authorities must seek any such direction from the High Court.
material_facts: The High Court had granted bail to the accused.
After bail was granted, the investigating authorities applied to the Magistrate for police remand, and the Magistrate authorized it.
The accused challenged the remand order.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate could not authorize police remand after the High Court had granted bail; the proper course was to approach the High Court, and the remand order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, after the High Court has exercised its authority to grant bail, the Magistrate's power to grant police remand ceases; any request for police remand must be made to the High Court. Such custody cannot be allowed for an undisclosed or flimsy reason, particularly where it would affect the liberty secured by bail. The Court applied the strict scrutiny required by Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the protections reflected in Article 22(2) of the Constitution and Section 57 of the Code.

predicates.post_bail_police_remand_request: The proceeding concerns a request to place an accused in police custody after bail has been granted.
predicates.high_court_granted_bail: A High Court had released the accused on bail before the custody request was made.
predicates.magistrate_authorized_police_remand: A Magistrate authorized police custody after the High Court granted bail.

issues.definition: When police custody is sought after a High Court grants bail and a Magistrate is asked to authorize it, only the High Court may authorize that custody.
